title: Should Animals Be Kept In Zoos?

blanks.sentence: School visits may help young people understand the value of _____.
Zoos may put money into _____ that support animals at risk.
These programmes are mainly used to help _____.
Female pandas can reproduce only during a _____ of fertility.
Some zoo funding is used to encourage difficult animals to _____.
Captive animals may show _____, suggesting poor mental health.
A zoo cannot fully copy an animal's _____.
Stress-related behaviour may include pacing, bar-biting and even _____.
Even big enclosures cannot give animals the _____ they would have in the wild.
For captive animals, even basic surroundings may be experienced as _____.

multipleChoice.question: What is presented as the main public reason zoos give for existing?
options: They educate young people about nature protection.
They provide entertainment for school groups.
They allow children to compare different gorillas.
They replace classroom science lessons.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the speaker mention visiting gorillas at Zoo Atlanta?
options: To show that zoos mainly attract local tourists.
To criticise repeated school trips to the same place.
To illustrate how zoos can introduce children to conservation.
To explain why gorillas are easier to protect in cities.

multipleChoice.question: According to the transcript, why may pandas need help with breeding?
options: They are too aggressive to live with other pandas.
They reproduce under limited conditions and may be unwilling to mate.
They cannot survive without human-made food.
They usually prefer warmer zoo environments.

multipleChoice.question: What role can zoo money play in panda conservation?
options: It helps pandas avoid contact with people.
It creates new wild habitats for pandas.
It trains pandas to live alone successfully.
It supports ways to encourage pandas to reproduce.

multipleChoice.question: What is the activist's first major objection to zoos?
options: They can harm animals both physically and psychologically.
They charge visitors too much money.
They focus too much on popular animals.
They fail to teach children enough science.

multipleChoice.question: Which behaviour is given as evidence that zoo animals may be under mental stress?
options: Sleeping for longer periods than usual.
Avoiding food offered by keepers.
Repeated movements such as pacing or head-bobbing.
Trying to communicate with visitors.

multipleChoice.question: What limitation of zoos is highlighted when they are compared with the wild?
options: Zoos cannot prevent all animals from escaping.
Zoos cannot truly reproduce animals' natural surroundings.
Zoos cannot stop visitors from disturbing animals.
Zoos cannot keep endangered species alive.

multipleChoice.question: What does the term connected with captive-animal stress refer to here?
options: A disease found only in polar bears.
A safety rule used in animal enclosures.
A training method used by zookeepers.
Repeated harmful behaviours caused by confinement.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the polar bear example used?
options: To show that polar bears are less intelligent than other zoo animals.
To suggest that polar bears are the only animals affected by captivity.
To make the habitat mismatch in zoos easier to imagine.
To prove that all large enclosures are equally cruel.

multipleChoice.question: What is implied by the comparison between zoochosis and human trauma?
options: Captive animals usually recover quickly if moved to larger spaces.
Captivity can create deep and continuous stress for animals.
Zoologists now treat animals with human medical methods.
Human trauma is easier to understand than animal behaviour.
